records.reported_effect: The crew detected smoke from containers on 13 August 2025 off West Africa; tugs reached the ship off Liberia and the spread was contained. After an expert team boarded on 19 August the voyage resumed. Maersk declared general average; the ship, earlier scheduled for China, was expected at Tanjung Pelepas, Malaysia, around 14 September, where cargo would be discharged and inspected.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The voyage was Europe to Asia, not on a case-study Asia to US lane; it is carrier-level context only. Cargo owners must post general-average security before delivery, which can delay release; the extent of damage was unknown at publication.
The source names Maersk; 'Maersk Line' is the graph carrier name used for matching. See approximations.
country_code is null because the fire occurred at sea off Liberia; the Malaysian discharge port is the destination, not the incident location.
No case-study shipment or booking on this vessel has been matched.

approximations.basis: Analyst mapping: the source attributes the vessel and general-average declaration to Maersk, recorded under the graph's carrier name 'Maersk Line' (SCAC MAEU). The source does not use that name.

search_window.note: Fire date to 14 days after the reported Tanjung Pelepas ETA, for retrieval only; not an observed recovery date.

records.disruption_type: service suspension driven by a customs rule change
records.reported_effect: Reuters, via the New Straits Times, reported that DHL Express would temporarily suspend shipments worth over US$800 to US consumers from 21 April 2025, after US formal-entry processing was required above US$800 (down from US$2,500 on 5 April). Business-to-business shipments over US$800 continued but could face delays. DHL resumed the consumer shipments on 28 April.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The resumption date is from Entrepreneur (29 April 2025), citing Reuters: https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/dhl-suspending-shipments-over-800-to-us-consumers/490322. DHL's own notice timed out on retrieval and was not reviewed.

The suspension covered express parcels to private individuals. Case-study shipments with carrier code DMAL are ocean bills of lading to Dyson business entities, which were B2B and not suspended; at most they faced possible clearance delays.
No delayed case-study shipment has been matched.

search_window.note: Suspension to resumption plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer.
